# TSLA Technical Analysis Report (as of 2026-11-11)

## 1. Data integrity

- The verified snapshot's latest row (2026-11-11) matches the `get_stock_data` row exactly: O 386.58 / H 395.43 / L 386.35 / C 390.84 / Vol 27,118,574.
- The snapshot values for 10 EMA, 50 SMA, 200 SMA, RSI, Bollinger middle, MACD and ATR match the `get_indicators` outputs. I found no discrepancies.
- **Not cross-checked:** VWMA (383.97) is not in the snapshot, so it is unverified against it. MACD signal (3.63), MACD histogram (-1.70) and the Bollinger upper/lower bands (418.70 / 344.97) come only from the snapshot, with no time series. I cannot describe their history.
- **Caveat:** the 11/11 bar is dated today. If the session is still open, its close, high, low and volume may still change.

## 2. Indicators chosen and why (8, complementary)

| Role | Indicator | Why it suits TSLA now |
|---|---|---|
| Short-term trend | close_10_ema | Price has swung sharply in recent weeks, and this tracks the quick shifts. |
| Medium-term trend | close_50_sma | Gives the intermediate trend direction and a reference level. |
| Long-term trend | close_200_sma | Price is oscillating around it, so it is the key strategic line. |
| Momentum/trend change | macd (with macds and macdh from the snapshot) | Shows momentum fading and rebuilding after the 11/04–11/05 sell-off. |
| Overbought/oversold | rsi | Registered a 35.81 low on 11/05 and has since normalized. |
| Volatility/range | boll (with the snapshot's upper and lower bands) | Defines the mean and the extremes of the current range. |
| Risk sizing | atr | Volatility rose materially in November, which matters for stops and position size. |
| Volume confirmation | vwma | Checks whether volume supports the price level. |

## 3. Price action context

**Longer backdrop (from the 129-row series):**
- Closes were in the 440s in mid-May (445.00 on 5/11, 445.27 on 5/13).
- On 7/23 the close fell to 319.69 from 374.01 the day before, on 115.6M shares, the heaviest volume in the dataset.
- The lowest close in the window was 298.32 on 7/29, with an intraday low of 297.38.
- From there price rebuilt through August and September into the 350–380 range.
- Late October brought a rally to 407.46 on 10/27. The highest recent high is 414.23 on 11/02.

**Last two weeks:**
- 11/02: close 403.82.
- 11/03: close 398.50.
- 11/04: gapped lower (open 379.80 vs prior close 398.50) and closed 385.19.
- 11/05: closed 343.69 on 79.7M shares, a drop of about 10.8% from 385.19, with an intraday low of 338.15.
- Since then price has rebounded in four straight sessions: 358.22, 378.05, 379.78, 390.84. That is about +13.7% from the 11/05 close.
- Today's open (386.58) was above yesterday's close (379.78), and the close was about +2.9% on the day.
- Volume has faded from the 11/05 spike (79.7M) to 27.1M on 11/11. The 11/11 figure is possibly partial (see section 1).

## 4. Trend analysis

**Moving averages**
- Close (390.84) is above all of: 10 EMA 381.20, 50 SMA 373.65, 200 SMA 383.03 and VWMA 383.97. It is also above the Bollinger middle, 381.83.
- **200 SMA reclaim is fresh and unconfirmed.** Closes on 11/09 (378.05) and 11/10 (379.78) were below the 200 SMA (383.51 and 383.23). 11/11 is the first close above it since the 11/05 sell-off. The last closes above it before that were 11/02 (403.82) and 11/03 (398.50). Price has crossed this line repeatedly, so one close is weak evidence of a regime change.
- **The 200 SMA is falling and the 50 SMA is rising.** The 200 SMA went from 390.07 (10/12) to 383.03 (11/11), while the 50 SMA went from 356.08 to 373.65. The gap between them narrowed from about 34 points to about 9.4. The 50 SMA is still below the 200 SMA, so there is no golden cross yet. If the current slopes persisted, they would converge, but that is not guaranteed and would depend on price holding up.
- **Confluence band at 381.20–383.97.** The 10 EMA (381.20), Bollinger middle (381.83), 200 SMA (383.03) and VWMA (383.97) all sit within about 2.8 points. This is a dense reference zone directly under price, and it should matter in either direction.
- The 10 EMA peaked at 394.27 on 11/03, fell to 378.90 on 11/09, and has recovered to 381.20. Price regained it on 11/10.

**Momentum**
- **RSI 54.36**, which is neutral. It ranged from 35.81 (11/05) up to 65.48 (10/27) over the window and did not reach 70. It went from near-oversold to mid-range within four sessions, so recent selling pressure has largely been absorbed. It does not signal an extreme either way.
- **MACD 1.93 vs signal 3.63, histogram -1.70.** MACD is still above zero but below its signal line, so the formal momentum read is still slightly negative even as price rebounds. MACD peaked at 9.59 on 11/02, fell to 1.12 on 11/10, and ticked up to 1.93 on 11/11. Because MACD lags, the price rebound has not yet turned the signal-line relationship positive. A MACD cross back above the signal would be the confirmation to watch for. I cannot say when it might occur.

**Volatility**
- **ATR 16.61**, about 4.2% of the close. It rose from about 11.04 (10/13) to 16.61, with the main step-up on 11/05 (16.44) after the sell-off. It has stayed elevated (16.68 on 11/10, 17.23 on 11/09).
- Bollinger bands are 344.97 (lower), 381.83 (middle) and 418.70 (upper). Price is above the middle, roughly 62% of the way from the lower to the upper band by my calculation. That is mid-to-upper range, not stretched.

**Volume**
- VWMA (383.97) is slightly above the Bollinger middle (381.83). The VWMA lookback is not stated, so I would not read much into the gap. Price is above VWMA, which is mildly supportive, but the rebound has come on much lighter volume than the sell-off.

## 5. Reference levels (descriptive only)

These come from tool data, and I make no claim about prior bounces or reactions.

**Above price**
- 395.43: today's high.
- 396.53 / 398.50: the 11/03 low and close. The 11/04 gap-down left an unfilled zone between its high (392.04) and the 11/03 low (396.53).
- 403.82–407.46: the 11/02 and 10/27 closes.
- 414.23: the 11/02 high.
- 418.70: Bollinger upper band.

**Below price**
- 381.20–383.97: the confluence cluster described above.
- 373.65: 50 SMA.
- 358.22 and 343.69: the 11/06 and 11/05 closes.
- 344.97: Bollinger lower band.
- 338.15: the 11/05 intraday low.

## 6. Scenarios (conditional, not predictions)

**Constructive case**
- Price holds above the 381–384 cluster and closes above 396.5, with the 10 EMA rising and MACD crossing back above its signal.
- The 50 SMA would keep rising toward the 200 SMA.
- The 11/02 high (414.23) and the upper band (418.70) would then become the next reference areas.

**Cautious case**
- A close back below the 381–384 cluster would turn today's 200 SMA reclaim into another failed attempt, as on 11/09 and 11/10.
- The 50 SMA (373.65) would be the next reference level, then the November low area.
- The negative MACD histogram, fading rebound volume and a still-declining 200 SMA would support this case.

## 7. Risk-management notes

- With ATR at 16.61, a 1.5× ATR distance is about 24.9 points and a 2× ATR distance is about 33.2 points. Measured from today's close, those equal roughly 365.9 and 357.6. These are illustrative arithmetic only, not recommended stops.
- Elevated ATR means stops tighter than about one ATR (about 16.6) sit inside recent normal daily movement. Position size should reflect the daily range, for example the 11/11 range of about 9 points and the 11/05 range of about 36 points (high 374.3, low 338.15).
- Gap risk is real, as shown by the 11/04 and 11/05 gaps and the 7/23 collapse.

## 8. Summary

The short-term picture is a sharp V-shaped rebound that has returned price above its key averages. Momentum confirmation lags: MACD is still below its signal, and the 200 SMA reclaim is only one close old. The next few sessions will show whether TSLA holds the 381–384 cluster and clears the 396–404 zone, or falls back into the prior range.

**Scope and data caveats**
- The tools return filings and vendor snapshots, not a "past week" news feed. The latest financial period is the quarter ended **2026-09-30 (Q3 2026)**. No insider transactions are dated within the last week. The most recent is **2026-09-08**, about 9 weeks ago.
- The income statement omits Q4 columns for 2021–2025. The cash flow statement is **cumulative year-to-date** (Q1, 6M, 9M). I derived discrete quarters by subtraction, and those figures are marked "derived".
- The balance sheet returns only six lines: assets, liabilities, cash and equity. There is no debt, inventory or receivables detail.
- Sector: Consumer Cyclical / Auto Manufacturers (NMS).

---

## 1. Valuation and market snapshot (vendor fundamentals)

| Implied price | ~$390.8 (derived: P/E 429.49 × EPS 0.91, and P/B 17.30 × BVPS 22.588 agree) |

- The implied price sits about 22% below the 52-week high and 31% above the low. It is about 5% above the 50-day average and 2% above the 200-day average.
- TTM profitability is thin:
  - Revenue is $103.6B and gross profit is $19.97B (19.3% gross margin).
  - EBITDA is $9.84B and net income is $3.22B (3.1% net margin).
  - Operating margin is 3.0%, ROE 3.8% and ROA 1.3%.
- Free cash flow (TTM, vendor) is $4.97B, a **~0.32% FCF yield** on market cap.
- The valuation rests almost entirely on expected future earnings growth, not current earnings.
- **Share count:** market cap ÷ price and equity ÷ BVPS both imply **~3.95B shares**. The weighted diluted count behind Q3 EPS is only about 3.5–3.6B (NI $787M ÷ EPS $0.22, rounding-sensitive). The gap may reflect the large June 2026 option exercise and unvested awards. This is worth verifying, because per-share metrics could understate dilution. On market cap ÷ net income, the TTM P/E is ~480x, not 429x.

## 2. Income statement trends (quarterly, USD millions)

| Quarter | Revenue | Gross profit | GM | Op income | Op margin | Net income | Dil. EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q3 2025 | 28,095 | 5,054 | 18.0% | 1,624 | 5.8% | 1,373 | 0.39 |
| Q1 2026 | 22,387 | 4,720 | 21.1% | 941 | 4.2% | 477 | 0.13 |
| Q2 2026 | 28,236 | 4,751 | 16.8% | 398 | 1.4% | 1,114 | 0.32 |
| **Q3 2026** | **28,046** | **5,494** | **19.6%** | **718** | **2.6%** | **787** | **0.22** |

**Q3 2026 results**
- Revenue was flat: -0.2% YoY and -0.7% QoQ. This follows +15.8% YoY in Q1 and +25.5% in Q2. Q2 2026 ($28.24B) is the highest revenue of any quarter in the data shown.
- Gross profit rose 8.7% YoY, and gross margin recovered 2.8 points QoQ.
- **Operating income fell 56% YoY** ($718M vs $1,624M). Implied operating expenses (gross profit minus operating income, derived) rose **~39% YoY** to $4.78B, and were up 9.7% QoQ. Opex has climbed every quarter shown:

| Quarter | Implied opex |
|---|---|
| Q3 2024 | $2.28B |
| Q1 2025 | $2.75B |
| Q3 2025 | $3.43B |
| Q1 2026 | $3.78B |
| Q2 2026 | $4.35B |
| Q3 2026 | $4.78B |

- Opex is now about 17% of revenue, versus about 12% a year ago. Cost growth, not demand, is the main drag on operating income.
- Net income ($787M) exceeded operating income ($718M), so non-operating items (likely interest income) and taxes helped. Net income fell 43% YoY and EPS fell 44%.
- **9M 2026 vs 9M 2025:** revenue $78.7B vs $69.9B (+12.5%). Net income was $2.38B vs $2.95B (-19.5%).
- **Implied Q4 2025** (TTM minus 9M, derived and approximate): revenue ~$24.9B, gross profit ~$5.0B (~20% margin), net income ~$0.84B.
- **Historical context:** the data shows a peak gross margin of 29.1% and operating margin of 17.2% (Q3 2022). Current margins are far below that.

- **Leverage:** vendor debt/equity is 18.3%, which implies roughly $16B of debt (derived). Total liabilities/assets rose to 42.9% from 39.6% a year ago. YoY, liabilities grew 27.6%, assets 17.8% and equity 11.6%.
- **Cause of the liability jump:** the +$6.6B QoQ rise is much larger than Q3 financing cash flow (+$0.3B). It is therefore likely payables or accruals, possibly tied to capex. Line-item detail is not available from these tools, so this is an inference only.

## 4. Cash flow (cumulative YTD; discrete quarters derived)

## 1. The V-shaped bounce is weaker than it looks

**The drop was not fully erased.** The bull measures from 11/04 (385.19). The sell-off started at the 11/02 close of 403.82, so the real drawdown to 343.69 was about 15%. The 200 SMA is falling partly because the high-priced Jan–Feb trading is rolling out of its window. Insider sales in that stretch were at $412–458. That is my inference, but a cross produced by windows rolling is not a buy signal.

**TSLA has now gapped down hard twice in 3.5 months.** On 7/23 it fell 14.5% on 115.6M shares, and on 11/05 it fell 10.8% on 79.7M. The July low was 298.32. The highs are also stepping down, from about 445 in May to 414.23 on 11/02. ATR is about 4.2% of price. This is a stock where overnight gap risk is a recurring feature, not a one-off.

**Nobody in this debate knows why it fell on 11/05.** The news feed failed. The bull says the market "tested TSLA and TSLA passed," but we can't say what the test was. A snapback after an unexplained drop is not a verdict on anything.

**The $400 weekly calls may be doing some of the lifting.** StockTwits shows 33,000+ contracts in the Nov 13 $400 calls. Open interest is unknown, and the source is low-confidence and partly promotional, so I'm not building on it. But a rebound propped up by short-dated call positioning is fragile once those contracts expire.

## 2. Q3 showed the cost base is outrunning the business

The bull leads with gross margin recovery. Gross profit rose about $440M YoY (5,494 vs 5,054). Implied opex rose about $1.35B over the same period (4.78B vs 3.43B). That is roughly $3 of added cost for every $1 of added gross profit.

The result was operating income down 56% YoY to $718M and operating margin of 2.6% vs 5.8%. Opex has risen in every quarter shown, from $2.28B in Q3 2024 to $4.78B, and is now about 17% of revenue vs about 12% a year ago. Nine-month net income is down 19.5% on revenue up 12.5%. The bull's "growth without profit growth" is the problem, not a defense.

Revenue went from +25.5% YoY in Q2 to -0.2% in Q3, and it fell 0.7% sequentially. Expect Q4 to show YoY growth, because the implied Q4 2025 comp is only about $24.9B. That would be an easy comparison, not reacceleration. Sequential growth is the tell to watch.

Net income ($787M) exceeded operating income ($718M), so the bottom line was helped by non-operating items and taxes.

## 3. The "investment phase" claim can't be tested

The bull admits the data doesn't show what the capex and opex buy. That makes "investment phase" unfalsifiable. What the data does show is:

- Capex is up 112% YTD, from 8.8% to 16.5% of revenue.
- Free cash flow is $1.9B vs $4.8B, down 61%, and Q2 FCF was negative (-$1.1B).
- ROE is 3.8% and ROA is 1.3%.

Spending doubled while operating income fell. If the returns were coming, they aren't in the numbers yet.

**The $6.3B Q3 operating cash flow needs a closer look.** Total liabilities rose $6.6B QoQ and current liabilities rose $5.1B (+14.3%). That is the same scale as Q3 OCF. My inference is that stretched payables or accruals flattered the quarter. The tools don't show line items, so the 10-Q needs to confirm it. If so, "OCF is 6x net income" is a timing benefit that can reverse.

Current ratio fell to 1.74 from 1.94. YoY, liabilities grew 27.6%, assets 17.8% and equity 11.6%. This isn't distress, but leverage is rising while profits fall.

## 4. Valuation leaves no cushion

I agree that valuation doesn't time a top. But the multiples set how large the shocks are:

- P/E is 429x trailing and 181x forward, with a PEG of 4.43 and an FCF yield of about 0.32%.
- Market cap is about 540x annualized Q3 operating income and about 157x TTM EBITDA (my arithmetic).
- Forward EPS of $2.16 is 2.4x TTM EPS of $0.91, and Q3 EPS of $0.22 annualizes to about $0.88. Delivering that growth while opex outgrows revenue is the assumption to test.

With no earnings anchor, 10–15% single-day moves are what you'd expect.

The implied share count of about 3.95B is above the 3.5–3.6B diluted count behind EPS. On market cap over net income, the trailing P/E is about 480x, not 429x. Per-share metrics may understate dilution.

## 5. The insider and macro arguments don't carry the bull's weight

**Musk:** The bull cites his ~$1.0B purchase at $371.90–396.36 "right where the stock trades today." That was in September 2025. The stock then fell to 298.32 in July and the data shows no purchase since. The June exercise of 304M options at $23.34 (~$7.09B) looks like exercising an old compensation award. It is not conviction buying. Whether it is dilutive depends on how it was settled, which means checking the Form 4. Otherwise the pattern is $87.7M of open-market selling in twelve months and no buys. I agree most of it looks programmatic, so I rate it neutral to mildly negative.

**Macro:** The bull calls it benign, but we have no CPI, yield, fed funds or unemployment data, and no TSLA headlines. The case rests on prediction markets. A 98% "no cuts in 2026" means no relief for a long-duration, rate-sensitive 181x stock or for auto affordability. A 2% recession probability doesn't help if the issue is margins and opex.

**Catalysts:** The bull says near-term catalysts are priced at zero (Optimus 3%, merger 10%), so surprises land on low expectations. At 181x forward earnings, expectations are not low. With no near-term catalyst, the stock has to rely on the Q3 fundamentals above. The merger odds are also thin-volume ($52K–$358K), and a merger would bring its own governance and dilution questions.

## Answering the bull's question

**Why was a 10.8% drop bought back in four sessions?** Dip-buying in a narrative stock tells you about positioning, not fundamentals. It also happened after a drop of unknown cause, partly on lighter volume, with options activity in the mix. Price still hasn't recovered its 11/02 level.

**What in Q3 supports "deteriorating" rather than "investing"?**
- Operating income fell 56% while revenue was flat.
- Opex is up 39% and gross profit only 8.7%.
- 9M FCF is down 61%, with negative FCF in Q2.
- Liabilities rose $6.6B in one quarter, and Q3 OCF may have been helped by that.

## What would change my mind

- Opex growth falling below revenue growth, with sequential revenue growth.
- Capex tied to disclosed, measurable returns.
- A clean close above 396.5 and then 404, with MACD crossing above its signal and the 200 SMA turning up.

## Bottom line

On the downside, a close back under 381–384 turns this into a third failed 200 SMA attempt. The next references are 373.65 (50 SMA), 358.22, then 343.69 and 338.15. At 429x trailing and a 0.3% FCF yield, I would not buy a stock with falling operating income, doubling capex and no earnings cushion on a one-close reclaim.
